about: Frozen test set for the agent router. Written BEFORE any candidate implementation exists, so no arm can be tuned against it after the fact. Every case marked source 'live-log' is a verbatim transcript Whisper actually produced during real use on 2026-08-09 — including its mishearings ('doc' for 'dock', 'Closed' for 'Close'), which are real input the router must survive. Cases marked 'constructed' fill coverage gaps for actions that were never exercised live.
scoring: Mechanical only. An arm passes a case when the produced action list matches `expect` on action name and on every argument listed. Arguments not listed are ignored. Never score by judging whether output 'looks reasonable'.

cases.guards: Simplest happy path, verified working today. Any arm that breaks this is disqualified regardless of other scores.
Second app to catch a name-specific fluke.
Lowercase app name plus trailing period. Never got a clean run today (rate-limited every attempt), so genuinely unmeasured.

Debatable and important: 'open settings' with no pane named should open the System Settings app, NOT route to open_system_setting with a bogus pane. The model got this right live and only failed on malformed syntax. If an arm routes this to a pane lookup it will hit the no-match fallback and now do nothing at all — a real UX regression introduced 2026-08-09.
Verified working today after initially looking broken (it was rate limiting, not a bug).
Whisper heard 'Closed' for 'Close'. Real ASR noise; the router should still read the intent.

cases.transcript: Find my latest resume in downloads folder.
cases.guards: Verified working today. Multi-argument extraction — the query must not swallow 'my latest' or 'folder'.
openFolder vs findFile is a genuine ambiguity — browsing a folder, not searching inside it.
Verified working today, and only after the matcher fix — this exact phrase was a NO MATCH before 2026-08-09.
Worked live. Pair it with settings-screen-time-implicit below: same destination, different phrasing, only one of them malformed.

The worst offender today: malformed tool call on every attempt including the higher-temperature retry, twice. If an arm fixes only one case, this is the one that matters. 'Show my X' phrasing without the word 'settings'.
Whisper heard 'doc' for 'dock'. The model DID map it to 'Desktop & Dock' correctly live — then malformed the wrapper. Tests semantic mapping through ASR noise.

Debatable expectation, recorded deliberately: macOS has no General pane (verified — it is a sidebar category), so 'general' is aliased to About, the first pane inside it. If we later decide a different target is better, change it HERE first, then re-run. Never measured live — every attempt was rate-limited.
Intent phrased as an action, not as 'open X settings'. Wallpaper was one of the panes the old hardcoded enum could never reach.
User-confirmed rule: 'password settings' means the Touch ID & Password pane, NOT the standalone Passwords app. Regression guard on an explicit product decision.
Must NOT become setWiFi. Viewing the pane vs toggling the radio — the pair with wifi-toggle-off below is the whole point.
Must NOT become openSystemSetting. Direct action takes precedence when a direction is stated.

KNOWN FAILING, deliberately. Two doors lead here. When the model punts to the Settings app, correctedSettingsPane now returns the visible fallback and this passes. When the model instead substitutes a real pane — 'banana' -> 'About', which is what it did on 2026-08-11 — nothing catches it. A rule that compared the model's pane against the spoken words did catch it, and also refused volume, brightness, dark mode, screensaver, microphone, camera, time zone and firewall, because the catalog lacks all of those and the right answers share no word with what was said. Nine real intents for one nonsense one; the rule was reverted. The durable fix is a synonym layer so the catalog resolves what people actually say, after which the comparison becomes safe. Until then this case stays red on purpose — see BACKLOG.md.
Enum argument extraction.
Same tool, different enum value — catches an arm that always picks the first enum member.
Boolean argument. Must not route to an Appearance pane open.
No-argument tool. Must not be confused with the Lock Screen settings pane.
No-argument tool, and the one irreversible action — a false positive here destroys data.
No-argument tool.
Question, not command. Must reach answerQuery rather than any side-effecting tool.

cases.transcript: How much storage do I have left
cases.guards: Must NOT open the Storage settings pane — asking a question vs opening a pane is a real confusion risk now that Storage exists in the catalog.
Query enum coverage.

cases.transcript: Open Safari, then tell me my battery
cases.guards: Two actions in one utterance, in order. Tool calling returns a native array; JSON mode needs our own array shape, so this is where arm B is most likely to differ.

Nothing matches — must return an empty action list, not force a bad fit into open_app. Tool calling gets this free via tool_choice auto; JSON mode needs an explicit empty-array convention in the prompt.

cases.transcript: Check my email for anything from a recruiter
cases.guards: Plausible-sounding but genuinely unbuilt capability. Tempting for a model to map onto open_app('Mail'), which would be wrong — the user asked to search, not to launch.
Bare open, no query, no flags. The simplest shape.

cases.transcript: Search for top rated iPhone 15 covers on Amazon
cases.guards: Widened after three runs scored 68/66/69 with this case flipping twice. Since the tool trim the model sometimes answers a search by putting the results URL in page_url alongside site — the same page either way. That form is now collapsed back to site+query in parseAction, so production is identical; the harness does not run parseAction and cannot see it, which is the third time that blindness has cost a cycle. Both shapes are correct AT THE MODEL LAYER, which is the only layer this eval measures, so the case asserts the site and leaves the query to eval/catalog-checks, whose nine decomposition cases pin the rebuilt URL exactly.

cases.transcript: look up Pranav Hari on LinkedIn
cases.guards: Person search. The whole query must land in `query`, not leak into `site`.

cases.transcript: Search for iPhone 15 Pro on Apple India website
cases.guards: Expectation corrected twice. First I expected site 'Apple India'; the model strips the country itself and region detection handles it. Then I expected search results; the model returns the iPhone 15 Pro product page, which is verified real and plainly better than Apple's own search. The lesson recorded rather than the guess.

cases.transcript: play a Kendrick Lamar song on youtube
cases.guards: play must be true here and absent for search — the verb is the only difference. Query wording is deliberately NOT scored: 'Kendrick Lamar' and 'Kendrick Lamar song' both work, and pinning the exact phrasing would fail on a difference that changes nothing.

Same widening as web-search-amazon. What this case actually guards is that 'search' does not become playback, so `play` must stay absent — that assertion is kept and is the part worth protecting; the query form is covered by catalog-checks.

cases.transcript: open the iPhone page on Apple India
cases.guards: Asserts only on the URL. The site label is unused when a page_url validates, and the model returns 'Apple India' or 'Apple' interchangeably — both resolve correctly, so pinning the label made a passing behaviour look like a regression.
NEW: same shape on a site with no search URL at all, where a deep link is the only way to be useful.

cases.transcript: look for people from Razorpay on LinkedIn
cases.guards: The People tab, not the mixed All tab. Today this lands on /search/results/all/ which buries people under posts and companies.

cases.transcript: look for product managers from Razorpay on LinkedIn
cases.guards: Role plus company. Same vertical as above — the difference is only the keywords, which is why query wording is not scored.

cases.transcript: find product manager jobs on LinkedIn
cases.guards: Jobs is a different URL entirely (/jobs/search/), not a tab on the same one.

cases.transcript: show me images of golden retrievers
cases.guards: No site named and a vertical implied by the word images. Two inferences at once.

cases.transcript: find swift concurrency repos on github
cases.guards: GitHub defaults to a mixed result page; repositories is usually what is meant.

cases.transcript: Search for iPhone page in Apple India website
cases.guards: THE case that failed live while the eval passed. Verbatim transcript. The word 'search' must not stop it reaching the canonical page — routing on the verb rather than on whether a real page exists was the bug.
Your own page on a site — a whole category missed until now. Orders, messages, subscriptions are canonical URLs that exist for every signed-in user.
Same category, different site.
No site named. Agreed default is Google rather than refusing.
Failed live: landed on LinkedIn search with 'my LinkedIn messages' as the keyword. The model had no page_url and no vertical matched, so it fell through to the ordinary search template.

Asserts only that the model identifies the site. The URL is not its job — it cannot see the Mac's region, so it will always write amazon.com. Our own table supplies the region-correct path and overrides whatever URL the model offered. That half is covered by eval/catalog-checks, which tests code rather than a model. Expecting amazon.in here was asking the model for knowledge it does not have.
YouTube has no regional variant, so this isolates the personal-page lookup from the region rewrite.

cases.transcript: search for wireless mouse on Amazon
cases.guards: Negative case for the personal-page table. An ordinary product search must not be captured by it — the table matches only when the query reduces to a bare intent word like 'orders' or 'cart'.

cases.transcript: Remind me to call the bank at 4pm
cases.guards: The title must not carry the time. 'call the bank at 4pm' as a title makes a reminder that reads wrong forever, and the time is already in its own field.

cases.transcript: Remind me to call the bank
cases.guards: The model must NOT invent a time. An invented due date is worse than none: the reminder fires at an hour nobody chose, and the follow-up question exists precisely to fill this in.

cases.transcript: Remind me to submit the form tomorrow morning
cases.guards: Relative phrasing only resolves because the current local time is in the system prompt. If this regresses, check that line is still being sent.
No name means the one just created. A name invented here would send the coordinator searching for a reminder nobody mentioned.
The word 'reminder' is noise and is stripped before matching, so it may or may not appear in the name — only 'dentist' matters.

cases.transcript: Remind me what my battery is at
cases.guards: 'Remind me' used conversationally, not as a command. Creating a reminder titled 'what my battery is at' would be a confident misread of a question.

The catalog has no pane called 'volume' — the model translates it to Sound and that is correct. Added after a rule was written that refused exactly this: it compared the model's pane against the spoken words and rejected anything with no shared root, which caught 'banana' and also broke volume, brightness, dark mode, screensaver, microphone, camera, time zone and firewall. Nine real intents for one nonsense one. The rule was reverted; this case exists so it cannot come back unnoticed.
Same class as settings-volume-synonym. 'brightness' is not in the catalog; Displays is the right answer and shares no word with what was said.

cases.transcript: Search for Type-C headphone on Flipkart
cases.guards: Verbatim from a live session where it was refused. Correct behaviour for an unknown site, and a US-centric gap: the catalog had Amazon and no Flipkart while the user is in India. URL confirmed in a browser — curl gets 403 from every Indian retailer, so a 403 proves nothing.

'Misho' is what the transcriber produces for Meesho, and it is the verbatim live transcript. The model maps it back to Meesho by itself once the site is in the vocabulary; the alias covers the case where it passes the misheard spelling straight through instead. First written with a site__contains matcher of 'isho', which 'Misho' satisfies and 'Meesho' does not — the expectation was wrong, not the routing.
The headline command. Zero-parameter tool, so there is nothing to malform.
Phrasing variety. FastRoute covers the common wordings locally; this proves the model still handles the ones it does not.
Reads the meeting back without joining it.
Asks the same question about time rather than identity; same tool.

MUST match nothing. Calendar writes are out of scope by an explicit design decision — a misheard word becomes a real event other people see. The danger is not a wrong meeting tool but an improvised create_reminder, which would silently turn a calendar request into a reminder.
MUST NOT route to cancel_reminder. Cancelling a meeting and cancelling a reminder are different destructive acts, and the reminder tool would happily search for a reminder named 'next meeting'.

cases.transcript: What meetings do I have today
cases.guards: DECISION REVERSED 2026-08-12, deliberately. The architecture had this declining rather than half-answering through next_meeting. Live experience overturned it: the wording that made the model refuse a list also made it refuse "check my calendar", which returned nothing at all and read as the feature being broken. Two attempts at wording that split the two failed in opposite directions. Answering with the next meeting is a partial answer to "what do I have today", and a partial answer beats silence — the person can see their calendar for the rest. The parked list surface is still parked; this is about not punishing an ordinary phrasing to protect a nicety.

cases.transcript: Remind me about the standup at 9am
cases.guards: Contains meeting words but is a reminder. Guards the boundary from the other side — the meeting tools must not attract everything that mentions a standup.

cases.transcript: Play a lo-fi song in YouTube
cases.guards: Verbatim from a live failure. 'in YouTube' rather than 'on YouTube' — the model answered with a page_url of the YouTube homepage instead of site+query+play, so it opened the front page and played nothing. web-play-flag covers the 'on' phrasing and passed throughout, which is why nothing caught this.

Declines, and that is accepted rather than desired. "play a song" names nothing to play — no artist, no genre, no title — so any choice would be invented. The phrasing that matters, "play a lo-fi song in YouTube", is covered by web-play-in-youtube and works. If this turns out to be common, the better answer is opening YouTube's music page rather than inventing a track, and that is a product decision nobody has made.

Live failure: answered nothing at all. The next_meeting description was tightened to refuse list-shaped questions after 'what meetings do I have today' half-answered — and that tightening reached too far, taking an ordinary way of asking what is next with it. The line has to reject a list without rejecting the question.
